product_brief: A feature in Fortanix Key Insight that helps organizations discover quantum risk, assess readiness, and prioritize threats for PQC migration.
pqc_capability_description: PQC Central is a feature embedded in Fortanix Key Insight within the Fortanix Armor platform. It facilitates end-to-end PQC readiness through discovery, risk assessment, and transition planning. It supports the adoption of quantum-resistant algorithms including Leighton-Micali Signature (LMS), Xtended Merkle Signature Scheme (XMSS), CRYSTALS-Kyber (ML-KEM), and CRYSTALS-Dilithium (ML-DSA) via Data Security Manager.
crypto_primitives: Leighton-Micali Signature (LMS), Xtended Merkle Signature Scheme (XMSS), CRYSTALS-Kyber (ML-KEM), CRYSTALS-Dilithium (ML-DSA)
key_management_model: Integrated with Data Security Manager (encryption and key management solution in Fortanix Armor); supports crypto agility without needing to upgrade or modify key management system or HSM deployment.
architecture_type: Application-layer feature embedded in Fortanix Key Insight; part of Fortanix Armor platform.
primary_platforms: On-premises and multi-cloud environments; integrates with IT Ops systems such as ServiceNow or Jira.
target_industries: Enterprise, Healthcare, Banking & Financial Services, Fintech, Manufacturing, Federal Government
pqc_roadmap_details: Enables building a PQC migration roadmap in enterprise IT Ops systems (ServiceNow, Jira); aligns with EU Member States’ roadmap to begin transition by end of 2026.
signature_schemes: Leighton-Micali Signature (LMS), Xtended Merkle Signature Scheme (XMSS), CRYSTALS-Dilithium (ML-DSA)
cryptographic_discovery_&_inventory: Scanning systems and services for cryptographic usage, mapping dependencies, cataloging assets using quantum-vulnerable algorithms, identifying vulnerable keys, and calculating a cryptographic readiness score.
deployment_&_migration_complexity: Facilitates seamless transition via Data Security Manager; allows tracking readiness across environments from a centralized dashboard; supports crypto agility without modifying key management system or HSM deployment.
organizational_readiness: Helps organizations turn PQC migration complexity into actionable insights and strategic priorities; provides clarity and control to take action now.

product_brief: Initial list of hardware and software categories supporting PQC standards to guide adoption and migration strategies.
pqc_capability_description: The framework lists product categories where manufacturer implementation and testing of PQC capabilities are encouraged. It covers technologies using PQC standards for key establishment (ML-KEM/FIPS 203) and digital signatures (ML-DSA/FIPS 204, SLH-DSA/FIPS 205, LMS, HMS, XMSS, XMSSMT). It does not list categories of PQC-capable products that are currently widely available, but rather those transitioning or expected to support PQC.
crypto_primitives: ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, LMS, HMS, XMSS, XMSSMT
infrastructure_layer: Application, Security Stack, Cloud, Hardware, Network
pqc_roadmap_details: Organizations are advised to prioritize acquiring PQC-capable solutions when planning purchases within listed categories. The list will be regularly updated. NIST Internal Report 8547 outlines the transition approach.
signature_schemes: ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, LMS, HMS, XMSS, XMSSMT

product_brief: Continuous cryptographic visibility and PQC readiness framework for cloud and code environments.
pqc_capability_description: Provides continuous visibility into cryptographic inventory, detects PQC-compliant Key Encapsulation Mechanisms (KEMs) like ML-KEM, identifies legacy algorithms (RSA, ECC, 3DES, RC4, SHA-1), and offers a PQC Readiness Framework for migration prioritization.
crypto_primitives: RSA, ECC, TLS, SSH, 3DES, RC4, SHA-1, ML-KEM
primary_platforms: AWS, Azure, GCP, multi-cloud, IaC, host configurations, CI/CD pipelines
pqc_roadmap_details: Framework categorizes findings into Legacy Resiliency, HNDL Risk, and Identity/Signature Resiliency; validates ML-KEM usage.
cryptographic_discovery_&_inventory: Yes; automatic discovery of algorithms, certificates, keys, libraries, and web services; supports CBOM creation; detects shadow cryptography and deprecated ciphers.
supply_chain_&_vendor_risk: Detects third-party libraries and container images; provides cryptographic bill of materials (CBOM).
deployment_&_migration_complexity: Supports continuous visibility, IaC scanning, and CI/CD guardrails to shift visibility left; aims to reduce architectural rigidity.
financial_&_business_impact: Included in Wiz Cloud and Wiz for Gov; no specific costs mentioned.
organizational_readiness: Provides PQC Readiness Champion Center and prioritized roadmap to assist teams in migration planning.

product_brief: A crypto agility platform for enterprise that automatically identifies and monitors cryptography systems with quantum vulnerability.
pqc_capability_description: S-CAPE automatically identifies and monitors cryptography systems with quantum vulnerability within IT systems. It supports migration to a post-quantum cryptography system through the Samsung Cloud Platform (SCP). The platform utilizes the AIMer algorithm, a PQC digital signature algorithm selected as a winner in the KpqC Competition, which is based on an internally developed one-way function.
crypto_primitives: AIMer (PQC Digital Signature), FIPS205 (SLH-DSA) (referenced for comparison)
pqc_roadmap_details: Samsung SDS plans to pursue standardization of the AIMer algorithm in line with domestic and international criteria. The company has piloted PQC application in the communication segments of SCP and will continue expanding the application. S-CAPE will be provided through SCP.
cryptographic_discovery_&_inventory: Automatically identifies and monitors cryptography systems with quantum vulnerability within IT systems.
constrained_device_&_iot_suitability: The AIMer algorithm is easier to be applied to lightweight devices, such as mobile and IoT devices, due to being 6.35 times faster and having a signature size 2.9 times smaller than FIPS205.

product_brief: A tool that captures TLS, QUIC, and SSH traffic to demonstrate how future adversaries could decrypt archived sessions using recovered ephemeral keys.
pqc_capability_description: The product is a simulation tool demonstrating vulnerability to future quantum attacks. It does not implement PQC; instead, it simulates the recovery of classical asymmetric keys (RSA, ECDLP) to decrypt sessions, highlighting the lack of PQC protection in current protocols.
crypto_primitives: RSA, ECDLP (Elliptic Curve Discrete Logarithm Problem), Curve25519, HKDF, PRF
key_management_model: Ephemeral private keys are exported from patched OpenSSL/OpenSSH during handshake to simulate key recovery; keys are stored in NSS keylog format for Wireshark decryption.
architecture_type: Software-based simulation tool (Python script with patched C libraries)
license: Not stated (LICENSE file present but content not provided in text)

product_brief: A toolset for dealing with Cryptography Bill of Materials (CBOM), including generation, visualization, and compliance checking.
pqc_capability_description: Features a foundational quantum-safe compliance check as a proof of concept. It evaluates cryptographic components against defined policies to identify quantum vulnerabilities. The internal service checks the quantum safety of asymmetric algorithms using whitelists of algorithm OIDs and names. It supports external evaluation via Open Policy Agent (OPA) using Rego policies.
crypto_primitives: Not stated (The tool scans for crypto usage but does not list specific primitives it implements; it detects JCA, BouncyCastle, pyca/cryptography, and Go crypto libraries)
architecture_type: Web frontend, API server, and database; supports deployment via Docker, Podman, and Kubernetes (Helm).
pqc_roadmap_details: The compliance framework is designed with extensibility in mind for implementing additional compliance checks and integrating custom compliance checks.
cryptographic_discovery_&_inventory: Generates CBOMs from source code by scanning private and public git repositories. Supports Java (JCA, BouncyCastle), Python (pyca/cryptography), and Go (crypto, golang.org/x/crypto). Provides visualization and statistics via CBOMkit-coeus.
supply_chain_&_vendor_risk: Generates Cryptography Bills of Materials (CBOMs) to inventory cryptographic assets. Supports SBOM topics.
deployment_&_migration_complexity: Supports production, coeus (standalone frontend), and ext-compliance (external OPA) deployment configurations.

pqc_capability_description: The document does not mention Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) support, algorithms, or migration plans.
